summary: US-007: Archived lifecycle state with domain events
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to archive a published performance so it stops appearing on the storefront while its history is preserved.

**Priority:** P1
**Depends on:** — (extends the TKT-26 publish machinery)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog exposes an idempotent archive transition (`published → archived`); archiving a draft is a 409 (only published offers archive); archiving an already-archived performance returns 200 without re-emitting — mirrors the publish idempotency precedent
- [ ] Archiving emits a versioned `platform.catalog.performance.archived` domain event with a deterministic envelope id (retried/raced emissions de-duplicate) so inventory can stop offering the slot; uses the existing poor-man's-outbox marker
- [ ] Archived performances disappear from the aggregated public list/detail reads; an event whose every performance is archived drops off the public list; TTL tiers unchanged (ADR-004)
- [ ] The lifecycle is a single explicit state machine (`draft | published | archived`) with rejected transitions returning 409 + a reason; unit + contract tests cover every edge

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; UI stories browser-verified with a screenshot in the PR; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002).

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

APIs are contract-first: the OpenAPI spec is the source of truth, served by the service at /openapi.yaml and checked for drift in the gate; domain events use a versioned platform envelope (id, type==subject, occurred_at, schema, data) published to JetStream with acks (never fire-and-forget), with a deterministic envelope id so retried/raced emissions de-duplicate.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog & event structure user stories (US-007…US-011)
ADR-005 unified dated-slot admission — the load-bearing abstraction this epic hardens; §Consequences names re-entry/mid-day-capacity/weather-closure as the pressure tests
M1 catalog baseline: 0001_catalog_schema.sql (organizers/venues/events/performances/ticket_types), publish + performance.published event, aggregated TTL reads

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed TKT-49 (US-007, archived lifecycle) — the owner prioritized it into Ready. Selection: of the two currently claimable TKT-2 children (TKT-49, TKT-50), TKT-49 was the one moved to Ready. It has **zero open blockers** and is a prefactor that **unblocks TKT-51 and TKT-52** (both are blocked-by it), so landing it first opens the most of the epic.

Branch `TKT-49-archived-lifecycle` cut off `origin/main` (aabf080, up-to-date base — local main was 1 behind). The TKT-2 PRD decomposition (US-007…US-011) is committed on the branch as a docs prep commit so it lands with the epic's first child.

Planning will preserve the existing idempotent-publish precedent: the archive transition mirrors publish (idempotent, deterministic-envelope-id emission via the poor-man's-outbox marker), extends the `draft|published` status into an explicit `draft|published|archived` state machine with 409+reason on illegal transitions, and filters archived slots out of the aggregated public reads without changing ADR-004 TTL tiers.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Draft execution plan — TKT-49 / US-007 (archived lifecycle state + domain event)

**Branch:** `TKT-49-archived-lifecycle`, based on `origin/main` at `aabf080` (+ the TKT-2 PRD docs commit `f17a776`).

### Definition of done
An organizer can archive a **published** performance through the catalog API. Archiving is idempotent (second call returns 200, no re-emit), flips `published → archived` in one atomic statement, and emits `platform.catalog.performance.archived` on the PLATFORM stream with a deterministic envelope id (retried/raced emissions de-duplicate). Archiving a **draft** is a 409 with a reason (only published offers archive). Archived performances disappear from the aggregated public list/detail reads; an event whose every performance is archived drops off the public list. TTL tiers are unchanged (ADR-004). The lifecycle is an explicit `draft | published | archived` state machine; every illegal transition returns 409 + reason. The M1 flow (US-002…006) stays green.

### Chosen test seam
Mirror the existing publish seam exactly — it is already proven and uses the same transition shape:
- **Unit (primary):** `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` — the `newEnv`/`fakeStore`/fake-publisher harness. Add archive cases mirroring `TestPublishEmitsExactlyOnceOnTransition` / `TestPublishRetriesEmissionAfterFailure` / `TestPublishUnknownPerformance` / `TestPublicListExcludesDrafts…`: emit-exactly-once-on-transition, idempotent re-archive (no second emit), archive-a-draft → 409, archive-unknown → 404, retry-after-emission-failure, and public-read exclusion (archived slot gone; all-archived event gone).
- **Real-Postgres smoke:** extend `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go` (`TestCatalogPublicationAndStorefront`) — after the existing publish + storefront assertions, subscribe a JetStream consumer on `platform.catalog.performance.archived` **before** archiving (same deliver-all-guard pattern used for publish), archive, assert 200 + idempotent re-archive + the archived envelope received, then assert the performance/event dropped from `/public/events`. The served-spec drift assertion already in this test covers the OpenAPI change.

No new test-only endpoint; no mutable status flag beyond the existing `status` column.

### Contract & data design
- **OpenAPI first** (`services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`, then `make generate`): add `POST /performances/{performanceId}/archive`, mirroring the publish operation. Responses: `200` (archived, returns the Performance), `404` (unknown), `409` (not archivable — still draft). Extend the `PerformanceStatus` enum with `archived`. Regenerate `openapi_gen.go` (never hand-edited) and refresh the embedded `api/spec.go`; the smoke drift check enforces byte-identity.
- **Migration** `0003_performance_archive.sql` (goose up/down, ADR-008 embedded):
  - Widen the status CHECK to `IN ('draft','published','archived')`.
  - Add `archived_at timestamptz` and `archive_emitted_at timestamptz` — a **second, independent** poor-man's-outbox marker. Rationale: `event_emitted_at` tracks the *publish* event's ack; reusing it for archive would make a published-then-archived slot unable to say which event is still owed. Parallel markers keep each transition's at-least-once retry independent (this is the main non-obvious design point; called out for review).
  - Down path: drop the two columns and restore the 2-value CHECK — but **fail closed** if any row is already `archived` (mirrors the TKT-30 down-migration precedent: never silently destroy lifecycle data).
- **Store** (`store.go` + `postgres.go`): add `ArchivePerformance(ctx, id) (Performance, needsEmit bool, err error)` and `MarkPerformanceArchiveEmitted(ctx, id)`. `ArchivePerformance` = single atomic `UPDATE performances SET status='archived', archived_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND status='published'`; on 0 rows affected, read the row to disambiguate not-found vs draft (→ new `ErrNotArchivable`) vs already-archived (idempotent: return the row, needsEmit from `archive_emitted_at IS NULL`). New sentinel `ErrNotArchivable`.
- **Public reads:** `publicPerformances` already filters `WHERE p.status='published'`, so archived falls out with **no query change**. I'll add tests to lock that behaviour (both slot-level and all-archived-event-level) so a future refactor can't regress it.

### Events (`events.go`)
- New `SubjectPerformanceArchived = "platform.catalog.performance.archived"`, `PerformanceArchivedData{PerformanceID, EventID, OrganizerID}` (no capacity — archive is a teardown signal). New `Publisher.PerformanceArchived(ctx, perf)`; `ArchivedEventID(perf)` derives the deterministic id from perf id + `archived_at` (mirrors `EventID`). Envelope schema starts at 1 for the new subject.

### API layer (`server.go`)
- `ArchivePerformance(w, r, performanceId)` mirrors `PublishPerformance`: call store; if `needsEmit`, publish then `MarkPerformanceArchiveEmitted` (same at-least-once + log-on-mark-failure semantics); map `ErrNotArchivable` → 409 in `writeStoreError`; return the Performance.

### Implementation sequence (TDD)
1. Write the OpenAPI archive operation + `archived` enum; regenerate; add the served-spec assertion is already present.
2. Unit tests first (red) in `server_test.go` for all archive cases incl. public-read exclusion.
3. Migration `0003` + store `ArchivePerformance`/`MarkPerformanceArchiveEmitted` + `ErrNotArchivable`; extend `fakeStore` to model archived.
4. `events.go` archived subject/data/publisher/id; extend the fake publisher in tests.
5. `server.go` handler + error mapping. Green unit tests.
6. Extend `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go` with the archive + exclusion assertions.
7. `make check` green. Browser: archive a published performance via API, refresh the storefront, confirm it's gone (screenshot for the PR).

### Explicit scope boundary
This story **emits** `performance.archived`; the **inventory consumer** reacting to it (stop offering the slot / tear down the pool) is TKT-4 — the existing `services/inventory/internal/consumer` subscribes only to `performance.published` and stays untouched here. Documented in the PR so the reviewer knows the consumer side is deliberately out of scope.

### Pre-mortem — assumed Gate-2/3 failure, and the guard
- **Reused outbox marker → after archiving, a publish-retry re-emits publish, or the archive event is never marked owed.** Guard: the **separate** `archive_emitted_at` column; unit test asserts archiving does not touch `event_emitted_at` and that archive retry-after-failure emits exactly once.
- **Race: two concurrent archive calls double-emit.** Guard: the single atomic `UPDATE … WHERE status='published'` flips exactly once; the loser sees 0 rows, reads back `archived`, returns idempotent 200 with `needsEmit=false`. Smoke asserts idempotent re-archive emits once.
- **Archived slot still leaks onto the storefront** (e.g. a cache serving the pre-archive body). Guard: the read query filters `status='published'`; test proves exclusion at slot and all-archived-event level. TTL means the storefront may show a stale archived slot until the ADR-004 minutes tier expires — that is the declared cache contract, not a bug; I'll note it in the PR (write-path invalidation is TKT-31).
- **Down migration destroys archived rows.** Guard: down fails closed if any row is `archived`, matching the TKT-30 precedent.
- **`draft → archived` allowed by accident**, stranding an unpublished slot in a terminal state. Guard: `WHERE status='published'` + the 409 test.

**Lens applied:** pre-mortem. It forced the separate-marker decision, the fail-closed down migration, and the explicit stale-cache note.

### Approval requested at Gate 2
Approve: the `POST /performances/{id}/archive` contract; the **separate `archive_emitted_at` outbox marker** (vs reusing `event_emitted_at`); `draft→archived` rejected as 409; archived-excluded-by-existing-published-filter (no read-query change); and inventory-consumer reaction deliberately deferred to TKT-4. No code lands before this passes cross-model review and is approved.

objective.note: Complete the draft/published/archived lifecycle (epic COS #2) by adding the archived state + its domain event; extends the TKT-26 publish machinery.

scope.note: IN: idempotent published→archived transition on a performance; versioned platform.catalog.performance.archived event with deterministic id (reuse the poor-man's-outbox marker); archived slots drop out of the aggregated public list/detail reads; explicit draft|published|archived state machine with 409+reason on illegal transitions. OUT: generalizing to other slot kinds (US-009/TKT-51), series/festival-level archive fan-out (US-010/011), inventory's reaction to the archive event (TKT-4 consumes).

uncertainties.note: Engineering choices settled in Planning, no product call: exact outbox/event-emitted marker reuse, whether archive is a new endpoint vs a state param, and how the public-read filter excludes archived without changing TTL tiers.

dependencies.note: No open blockers — extends TKT-26 (Done). Blocks TKT-51 and TKT-52 (they carry the lifecycle onto every slot kind / series).

approach.note: Mirror the existing idempotent publish handler + deterministic envelope-id emission in services/catalog; add an archived status value + a lifecycle state-machine guard; filter archived from the aggregated public queries. Contract-first: OpenAPI updated, drift check in the gate (ADR-009).

first_slice.note: The story is one reviewable vertical slice: archive a published performance via API → event emitted → it disappears from the storefront read, browser-verifiable alone.

success.note: COS = the 4 ACs + quality gates (make check green, contract tests on the catalog boundary, ADR-004 tiers unchanged).
